description: Evidence table for reminder TYPE classification. Each type accumulates a score from its 'evidence' rows (evaluated in order; a row with 'only_if_no_other_evidence' counts only when no earlier evidence row of the same type matched); 'support' rows are corroboration that is added only when at least one evidence row matched — support can never reach the threshold alone. A row matches when its 'pattern' (a case-insensitive-by-(?i) regex FRAGMENT run against the body) and/or its 'sender_table_ref'/'table_ref' regex match; 'table_ref'/'sender_table_ref' reference the assembled regexes from tables/billers.json ('insurer_names', 'bill_domains', 'known_biller_senders') so brand lists live in one place. 'not_if_guard' names a guard from guards.json whose match suppresses the row (e.g. product-tier 'Premium' never counts as an insurance premium). The SCORING ALGORITHM — the threshold (3), the tie-break order (credit card, deposit, EMI, insurance, bill, subscription), and bill-evidence disqualifying subscription — stays in code (ReminderTypeClassifier); only pattern content and weights live here. Keep patterns simple: word boundaries, bounded gaps like [^\n]{0,60}?, never nested quantifiers; patterns are ReDoS-validated at load and invalid rows are skipped.

evidence.comment: The bill's OBJECT is the credit card itself ('Your credit card bill for Federal Bank XXXX-1234') - weighted above the generic bill-domain words ('fees', 'tax') that a card bill's late-fee advisory also mentions, so a card bill from an aggregator (CRED) types as CREDIT_CARD, not generic BILL.

Indian card issuers brand the product as one word - BOBCARD, SBICARD, ONECARD - so 'Statement for BOBCARD **1234' never matched the 'card statement' / 'statement for your card' wordings and typed as OTHER. Anchored on 'statement for' so a bare brand mention cannot score.

Prepaid plan/pack/validity expiry recharge notices ('Your plan ... is expiring today. Recharge IMMEDIATELY ...'): the recharge IS the obligation, so the expiry types as a generic bill reminder - the same family as the Airtel pack-expiry and ACT recharge precedents. Anchored on all three legs (the plan/pack/validity subject, its expiry verb, AND a recharge call-to-action AFTER it) so a promo's 'offer expires' with a leading 'Recharge with Rs.299 plan' or a voucher lapse never types.
